Full Q&A on the page — Question: "Where is Section 161LG Row O at Dodger Stadium?" Answer: "Loge Section 161 is located between 3rd base and the left field foul pole, and is closer to the outfield (please note that the LG suffix in the section you listed stands for Loge). There are 19 totals rows in the section, running from Row A to Row T (no rows at I or Q), and is followed by Row W which is designated for handicapped seating. Row O will be the 14th row of the section, and is 32 rows from the field as section 49 is located between section 161 and the field. There are 19 total seats in row O, with seat 1 being furthest to the right as you face the field." CONTRADICTION within the page: the row-label line says "Rows in Section 161 are labeled A-T, U-W" (i.e. rows U, V and W exist), while the Q&A answer says the section runs "from Row A to Row T (no rows at I or Q), and is followed by Row W which is designated for handicapped seating" — the Q&A omits rows U and V and calls W handicapped seating. Fan review, Sec 163 / Row E • Baseball: "Really cool perspective of the game — I'm a sucker for seats that look straight in on homeplate down a foul line - especially in left field. There's just so much action that comes this direction that you almost feel like you're playing left field and a part of the game. The only problem is that in order to get your down the line view, you have to look right the whole game. If you sit in your seat and look straight ahead, you're looking at RF. This can be a little bit straining after a while. Among Loge level seats, Section 163 certainly isn't the greatest. You're 350 feet from home plate and the rows have more seats than most. But if you want to be on the loge level and can only afford seats down the line, these are way better than seats in right field where the sun will be in your face. Real close to stairs leading to LF plaza and bar, which is super-awesome. Hang out there during batting practice then head up to your seats for the game." No Q&A on the page.
